senses.gloss: A tax charged on goods brought into a country.
examples: Travelers pay *duty* on anything worth more than eight hundred dollars.
Congress raised the *duty* on imported steel.
The shop past security sells perfume with no *duty* added.

senses.gloss: A machine that turns motion into electric current.
examples: The bike's headlight runs off a little *dynamo* on the front wheel.
The mill drove a *dynamo* that lit the whole village.
Two old *dynamos* are still bolted to the floor of the plant.

senses.gloss: A sports team or club that stays dominant for many years.
examples: Five titles in seven years made them a *dynasty*.
Fans still argue about which *dynasty* was the greatest.
He built a *dynasty* at a school nobody had heard of.

senses.gloss: A golf score of two strokes under par on one hole.
examples: He sank a long putt for an *eagle* on the par five.
Two *eagles* in one round is almost unheard of.
Her *eagle* on the sixteenth won the tournament.

senses.gloss: The part of a corn or grain plant that holds the kernels.
examples: We grilled six *ears* of corn on the coals.
Each stalk carries one or two good *ears*.
She pulled the husk off the *ear* and salted it.

senses.gloss: A natural ability to hear and judge sounds.
examples: She has a good *ear* for languages.
He never took lessons; he plays by *ear*.
That producer has an *ear* for a hit song.

senses.gloss: The part of a country or of the world that lies in that direction.
examples: He grew up in the *East* and moved to California at twenty.
Storms roll off the plains and hit the *East* by morning.
Trade between the *East* and the West goes back centuries.

senses.gloss: The cheapest class of seats on a plane or train.
examples: We flew *economy* both ways to save money.
*Economy* was full, so they moved us up front.
Even in *economy* every seat now has a screen.

senses.gloss: Careful use of money or resources so that nothing is wasted.
examples: Buying the cheap boots turned out to be a false *economy*.
The airline is hunting for *economies* in its fuel bill.
There is real *economy* in cooking one big pot on Sunday.

senses.gloss: An illegal drug that makes users feel energetic and affectionate.
examples: Police found *ecstasy* in the glove compartment.
*Ecstasy* is common at all-night dance parties.
The pills he bought turned out not to be *ecstasy* at all.

senses.gloss: An advantage over other people or over a rival.
examples: Speaking Spanish gave her an *edge* in the interview.
The company lost its *edge* to cheaper competitors.
A full night's sleep is a real *edge* on game day.

senses.gloss: A sharp, angry quality in someone's voice.
examples: There was an *edge* in his voice when he answered.
She asked a second time, this time with an *edge*.
His jokes always have an *edge* to them.

senses.gloss: The work of cutting and arranging film or video into its final form.
examples: The *editing* in the chase scene is brilliant.
She spent a month on the *editing* of the documentary.
Sloppy *editing* made the interview look choppy.

senses.gloss: A computer program used for writing and changing text or code.
examples: Open the file in a plain text *editor*.
Most *editors* underline your mistakes as you type.
He still swears by the *editor* he learned in college.

senses.gloss: The person who cuts and arranges the shots in a film.
examples: The *editor* trimmed twenty minutes out of the movie.
*Editors* rarely get the credit they deserve.
She works as a film *editor* in Los Angeles.

senses.gloss: An artificial sound or image made for a film, show, or recording.
examples: The *effects* in that movie cost more than the cast.
A radio play lives or dies on its sound *effects*.
The rain in the last scene was an *effect*, not real water.

senses.gloss: The personal belongings a person carries or leaves behind.
examples: The hospital returned his personal *effects* in a paper bag.
She packed her few *effects* and left before dawn.
Officers listed every one of the *effects* found in the car.

senses.gloss: A pipe fitting bent at an angle to turn a line in a new direction.
examples: You'll need a ninety-degree *elbow* under the sink.
The plumber soldered a copper *elbow* onto the line.
Two *elbows* carry the vent around the beam.

senses.gloss: One of the parts or qualities that make up a whole.
examples: There's an *element* of risk in any investment.
The story has all the *elements* of a good thriller.
An *element* of truth ran through the rumor.

senses.gloss: The weather, especially when it is cold, wet, or rough.
examples: A tarp protects the stacked wood from the *elements*.
The hikers were out in the *elements* all night.
Old barns take a beating from the *elements*.

senses.gloss: The metal coil that produces heat in a stove, oven, or water heater.
examples: The *element* in the water heater burned out.
One *element* on the stove no longer glows red.
Replacing an oven *element* takes about ten minutes.

senses.gloss: A large group of businesses controlled by one person or company.
examples: She built a beauty *empire* out of her own kitchen.
The family's media *empire* includes four newspapers.
His restaurant *empire* fell apart in under a year.

senses.gloss: A hard glossy coating baked onto metal or pottery.
examples: The *enamel* on the old bathtub is chipped.
She collects blue *enamel* camping mugs.
*Enamel* paint holds up well on a porch railing.

senses.gloss: A goal that someone is trying to reach.
examples: The money is only a means to an *end*.
To that *end*, we hired two more people.
He'll use anyone to serve his own *ends*.

senses.gloss: The way a story, film, or event finishes.
examples: The book has a surprisingly happy *ending*.
Don't tell me the *ending*.
Both *endings* were filmed and shown to test audiences.

senses.gloss: A locomotive that pulls a train.
examples: The *engine* hauled forty cars over the pass.
Two *engines* were needed for that grade.
The kids waved at the *engine* from the crossing.

senses.gloss: Something that drives growth or change.
examples: Small business is the *engine* of the local economy.
Cheap oil was the *engine* behind the boom.
Immigration has long been an *engine* of growth.

senses.gloss: Something submitted to a competition.
examples: Her photo of the barn was the winning *entry*.
The fair received over three hundred *entries* this year.
Late *entries* will not be judged.

senses.gloss: A single event or short period in someone's life.
examples: He'd rather forget the whole *episode*.
The *episode* at the airport made the evening news.
It was an ugly *episode* in the town's history.

senses.gloss: A period when an illness or condition flares up.
examples: She had another *episode* of dizziness at work.
The medication cuts the number of *episodes* in half.
His first *episode* put him in the hospital for a week.

senses.gloss: Fairness in the way different people are treated.
examples: The district is rewriting its budget with *equity* in mind.
Pay *equity* was the union's main demand.
They talk about *equity*, not just equal treatment.

senses.gloss: Shares in companies, held as an investment.
examples: His retirement savings are mostly in *equities*.
The fund moved money out of *equities* and into bonds.
Over thirty years *equities* have done better than bonds.

senses.gloss: The gradual weakening or loss of something valued.
examples: The scandal caused a slow *erosion* of trust.
Judges warned of a steady *erosion* of basic rights.
Inflation means the quiet *erosion* of everyone's savings.

senses.gloss: Something that lets you forget your troubles for a while.
examples: For her, gardening is an *escape*.
Movies were his only *escape* that winter.
Cheap paperbacks offer a quick *escape* on a long flight.

senses.gloss: A concentrated liquid taken from a plant and used for flavor or scent.
examples: Add a teaspoon of vanilla *essence* to the batter.
The shop sells *essences* of lemon, almond, and rose.
One drop of peppermint *essence* is plenty.

senses.gloss: The invisible air or space in which signals travel and things seem to vanish.
examples: My email must have disappeared into the *ether*.
Their promises vanished into the *ether* after the election.
The signal goes out into the *ether* and comes back a second later.

senses.gloss: The moral rules that govern a profession, or the study of right and wrong.
examples: Medical *ethics* forbid discussing a patient's file.
The company published a code of *ethics* last spring.
She teaches *ethics* at the law school.

senses.gloss: A single race or contest within a larger sports meeting.
examples: She's entered in three *events* at the state meet.
The 400-meter *event* starts right after lunch.
Skiing has more Olympic *events* than it used to.

senses.gloss: A particular harmful thing or practice.
examples: He called the plan the lesser of two *evils*.
Reformers set out to fight the social *evils* of the day.
For most farmers, debt is a necessary *evil*.

senses.gloss: A careful check of the body carried out by a doctor.
examples: Her yearly *exam* is on Tuesday morning.
The eye *exam* took about twenty minutes.
Every player needs a physical *exam* before the season.

senses.gloss: Someone or something held up for others to copy or to learn from.
examples: Her father set an *example* of hard work.
Coaches are supposed to be an *example* for the kids.
The judge made an *example* of him with a heavy fine.

senses.gloss: The pipe and muffler that carry burned gas away from an engine.
examples: The *exhaust* rusted through and now the truck roars.
He put a new *exhaust* on the car last weekend.
Both *exhausts* on that sports car are chrome.

senses.gloss: A place where cars leave a highway.
examples: Take *exit* 42 and turn left at the light.
We missed our *exit* in the rain.
The next two *exits* are closed for construction.

senses.gloss: The act of leaving a place, a job, or a stage.
examples: She made a quiet *exit* before the speeches started.
His *exit* from the company surprised everyone.
Reporters kept asking about the coach's sudden *exit*.

senses.gloss: The small hole at the end of a needle that the thread goes through.
examples: I can't get the thread through the *eye*.
Hold the needle up so the *eye* catches the light.
The *eyes* on these needles are too small for yarn.

senses.gloss: The calm center of a hurricane.
examples: The *eye* passed directly over the island.
The wind died for half an hour when the *eye* arrived.
Satellite pictures showed a clear, round *eye*.

senses.gloss: An ability to notice or judge things well.
examples: She has an *eye* for color.
It takes a good *eye* to spot a fake.
He has an *eye* for hiring the right people.

senses.gloss: A light cotton fabric with small holes stitched into a pattern.
examples: The blouse is made of white *eyelet* with a scalloped hem.
The curtains are trimmed with *eyelet*.
*Eyelet* is cool to wear in August.

senses.gloss: A false outward appearance that hides how someone really feels.
examples: He kept up a *facade* of calm all through dinner.
Her cheerfulness was a *facade*.
The *facade* cracked when they asked about the money.

senses.gloss: The front or outer surface of an object.
examples: The clock *face* is cracked but it still runs.
Climbers spent two days on the north *face*.
Water runs down the *face* of the dam.

senses.gloss: An expression made by moving the mouth and eyes.
examples: The kid made a *face* at the broccoli.
She pulled a *face* when she heard the price.
Quit making *faces* at your sister.

senses.gloss: Respect or dignity in the eyes of other people.
examples: He took the deal to save *face*.
Nobody wants to lose *face* in front of the whole team.
The apology let both sides keep *face*.

senses.gloss: A whole number that divides exactly into a larger number.
examples: Three is a *factor* of twelve.
List all the *factors* of thirty-six.
The two numbers share no common *factor* but one.
